summary: Written information security program with a Qualified Individual, risk assessment, access controls, encryption, MFA, pen testing/vuln scanning, IR plan, board reporting; plus FTC breach notice (314.4(j)).
applies_to: Non-bank financial institutions, which 16 CFR 314.2 says expressly include 'an accountant or other tax preparation service that is in the business of completing income tax returns.'
size_thresholds: 314.6: institutions holding customer information on fewer than 5,000 consumers are exempt from 314.4(b)(1) (written risk assessment), (d)(2) (continuous monitoring/pen testing), (h) (written IR plan) and (i) (annual board report). The 314.4(j) FTC notice applies only to events affecting 500 or more consumers.
status: In force. Most 2021 amendments effective June 9, 2023; 314.4(j) effective May 13, 2024 (314.5).

summary: Criminal penalty (misdemeanor, up to 1 year and/or $1,000) for preparers who knowingly or recklessly disclose or use tax return information except as permitted.
applies_to: Tax return preparers, including CPA firms and preparation services.

summary: IRS guidance on the security measures tax professionals should take and on meeting the FTC Safeguards Rule. IRS says a data security plan 'isn't just a good idea, it's federal law.'
applies_to: Tax professionals (the legal duty comes from 16 CFR 314).
size_thresholds: Scales to firm size (per the Safeguards Rule).
status: Guidance; Pub 4557 Rev. 5-2024 current on irs.gov.

summary: 15 basic safeguarding controls for contractor systems that process, store or transmit Federal Contract Information (FCI).
applies_to: Federal contractors and subcontractors at any tier whose systems may hold FCI.
size_thresholds: No size threshold. Does not apply to acquisitions solely of COTS items (FAR 4.1902).
status: In force (clause dated NOV 2021). FAR CUI proposed rule (Jan 15, 2025) and FAR cyber incident reporting proposed rule (Oct 3, 2023) remain proposed. A 'Revolutionary FAR Overhaul' proposed rule was published June 23, 2026. FAR overhaul: under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation (adopted by DoD, GSA, DHS, DOE, VA and most other agencies; list read on acquisition.gov 2026-10-08), new solicitations and awards carry FAR 52.240-93, Basic Safeguarding of Covered Contractor Information Systems, with the same 15 requirements and flow-down. Contracts awarded earlier keep FAR 52.204-21 until modified.

summary: Protect Covered Defense Information per NIST SP 800-171, report cyber incidents to DoD within 72 hours, and hold the CMMC level required by the solicitation at award.
applies_to: DoD contractors and subcontractors handling FCI or CUI.
size_thresholds: No small-business exemption. The CMMC level (1-3) is set per contract.
status: In force. The CMMC program rule is 32 CFR 170. The DFARS CMMC acquisition rule (90 FR 43560) took effect Nov 10, 2025 with phased implementation.

summary: Firms that create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI for a covered entity must meet the Security Rule directly, sign BAAs, and report breaches to the covered entity.
applies_to: Service firms handling PHI: law firms, CPAs/auditors, IT/MSPs, billing firms, call centers, staffing firms placing clinical staff, and similar.

citation: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct (model rules, NOT law; binding only as adopted by each state's highest court)
summary: Technology competence (understand the benefits and risks of relevant technology) and reasonable efforts to prevent unauthorized access to or disclosure of client information.
applies_to: Lawyers and law firms, to the extent their state has adopted the rule.
status: Model rules; state adoption varies. Could not fetch the ABA site (HTTP 403).

short_name: AICPA Code of Professional Conduct - Confidential Client Information
citation: AICPA Code ET sec. 1.700 (professional standard, NOT law; incorporated by many state boards of accountancy)
summary: CPAs must not disclose confidential client information without consent. SOC 2 (Trust Services Criteria) is the de facto attestation for service organizations.
applies_to: AICPA members / licensed CPAs (per state board adoption).
status: Professional standard. Not verified from the source.

summary: Would require covered entities to report covered cyber incidents to CISA within 72 hours and ransom payments within 24 hours (proposed 226.5).
applies_to: IT entities and DoD contractors, among others: proposed 226.2(b)(4) (contractors required to report under DFARS 252.204-7012) and (b)(12) (certain IT entities), or any CI-sector entity exceeding its SBA size standard.
size_thresholds: Proposed 226.2(a): entities in a CI sector that exceed the SBA small-business size standard for their NAICS code (13 CFR 121), or that meet a sector-based criterion regardless of size.
status: PROPOSED ONLY. NPRM 89 FR 23644 (Apr 4, 2024). CISA held town halls (Feb 13 and May 26, 2026 notices) to refine scope. Fall 2025 Unified Agenda targeted a final rule for 09/2026. As of 2026-09-25 no final rule is in the Federal Register; CISA says it 'continues to work on the final rule.' Reporting is not yet mandatory.
